A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable versions of EF-3DGS with matching core methods, experiments, equations, and figures. v3 ends with references; v4 additionally contains a checklist and Appendix A. All supplied material supports reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 5 reports original rendering and camera-pose experiments on Tanks and Temples and RealEv-DAVIS, including component ablations and pose-perturbation tests.

after.justification: v4 retains those empirical results and additionally reports blur, harder-speed, sensitivity, computational-efficiency, and color-correction experiments in Appendix A.

M1.justification: The core EGM, CMax/LEGM, PBA, and Fixed-GS procedure is retained. Appendix A.1 adds an EDI+EF-3DGS variant for blurred inputs, replacing the intensity term in Equation 5 with an EDI-based sharp-intensity estimate in Equation 19.

E1.justification: The datasets and reconstruction tasks are retained, while v4 extends evaluation to motion-blurred Tanks and Temples inputs and a more severe FASTER condition on RealEv-DAVIS. These are bounded extensions of the tested input conditions.

E2.justification: The main comparison tables retain their baselines. Appendix Table 8 adds ENeRF to the RealEv-DAVIS comparison, although it already appeared on Tanks and Temples, and Table 11 introduces COLMAP+3DGS.

E3.justification: The retained experiments preserve their stated frame rates, test-frame selection, metrics, and main hyperparameters. Added protocols include gamma correction and 30-frame averaging for blur at 2 FPS, every-tenth-SLOW-frame sampling for FASTER, and parameter sweeps with training-time and rendering-speed measurements.

E4.justification: Beyond v3's component ablations and pose-perturbation test, v4 provides blur robustness, warping-window and loss-weight sensitivity, subinterval accuracy-versus-cost analysis, COLMAP registration-failure analysis, and an alternative color-loss comparison against Fixed-GS. Additional depth, warped-event, and color visualizations expand the diagnostic evidence.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, significance tests, or statistical error bars. v4's checklist explicitly acknowledges the absence of statistical-significance reporting without introducing a different reporting practice.

E6.justification: All numerical content in Tables 1-4 is unchanged. v4 adds substantial results, including per-scene RealEv-DAVIS scores, sensitivity and runtime measurements, 23.18 dB PSNR for EDI+EF-3DGS under blur in Table 5, and 20.18 dB for EF-3DGS under FASTER in Table 11. These are additional results under newly reported conditions.

T1.justification: Equation 19 adds the EDI-based mathematical formulation used to replace the latent intensity term for blurred inputs. The original mathematical development in Equations 1-18 is retained apart from notation corrections; no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same novelty claim, core components, and headline claims of up to 3 dB higher PSNR and 40% lower ATE. The expanded conclusion reiterates these contributions.

C2.justification: v4 distinguishes blur handling from the sparse-view and pose-estimation problem, explains parameter sensitivity through motion assumptions and constraint balance, and interprets Fixed-GS as an efficiency choice when an alternative color loss also works. Appendix A.9 newly states the requirement for ordered inputs and potential manual parameter tuning, substantially expanding applicability and limitations discussion.

D1.justification: v4 adds Algorithm 1, local/global Gaussian initialization and 50-frame allocation details, sequence statistics, RTX2080Ti timing information, and access/licensing statements with a promised code and dataset release. These expand documentation without establishing reruns of retained experiments. Sequence duration remains ambiguous between the main text's 40-second RealEv-DAVIS recordings and Appendix A.2's 50-second segment statement.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds references to EMotive, Event-based Tracking Any Point, and URNet while retaining the existing cited works after renumbering. The appendix further contrasts the approach with deblurring-focused reconstruction, preserving its central positioning around joint pose and scene optimization.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and section order are preserved. v4 makes localized wording and notation edits, reverses the dataset-results paragraph order, expands the conclusion, and adds contact/conference information, acknowledgements, a checklist, and organized appendix sections.

P2.justification: The two-column layout becomes a single-column NeurIPS format, with retained displays resized and relocated. Tables 5-12, Algorithm 1, and Figures 7-19 add substantial tabular, sensitivity, ablation, and expanded qualitative displays. The original embedded figure assets are retained.

improvement.justification: v4 substantially improves the paper's self-contained documentation and validation. Algorithm 1 and the practical allocation details clarify long-sequence implementation, while the blur, harder-speed, sensitivity, and color-correction studies examine important failure modes and justify design tradeoffs. Explicit limitations also clarify applicability. These gains are substantial despite unchanged headline results, continuing absence of statistical uncertainty, and the sequence-duration ambiguity.
